**What changed**

- **Model.** Your user settings now set the environment variable `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL` to `fable`, the same alias your main session uses, so every subagent defaults to Fable 5.1. This is the only documented global switch.
- **Effort.** There is no global effort switch for subagents. They inherit the session's effort, which is high for you. The only documented override is the `effort` field in a named agent definition. So the worker seat is now a named agent in the repo at `.claude/agents/worker.md` with model fable and effort medium. Its body is the standing worker preamble from hybrid.md, moved verbatim, so it no longer has to be pasted ahead of every brief.
- **hybrid.md** carries a dated note at the top, the worker seat now reads Fable 5.1 at medium, the preamble section points at the agent file, and the economics section is marked superseded. The Aug 16 Opus comparison stays as the record of why the seats were split.
- **Memory** updated so future sessions know the worker seat and how to spawn it.

**Two things to know**

- Subagents I spawn without a named type, such as Explore or general-purpose, will run Fable at high effort, not medium. If you want medium everywhere, the fix is to spawn everything as `worker` or a second named agent. Whether a same-named file can override a built-in type is undocumented.
- The docs do not say whether the env var accepts the `[1m]` context suffix, so workers get the standard context window until we test it.

### p4
*2026-09-02 09:24*

> the next thing is that I'd like to find ways to speed up the workflow that leads to a release. I wonder if the enable/disable check can be skipped by enforcing certain patterns in the work.

This is a design question, so no node. Let me look at what the toggle proof actually costs today and what the linker already knows, then give you a proposal.

Yes. The toggle proof can be skipped whenever the commit fits one pattern, and the argument is exact, not approximate.

**What the toggle proof actually checks.** Untick the node, relink, confirm the code left, confirm nothing else broke. The linker never reads an unticked node's files. So the composition without the node is determined entirely by every file outside the node's directory. If none of those changed, the composition without the node is byte for byte the composition of the previous commit. That commit already built, passed the smoke gate, and shipped. Re-proving it is what the toggle proof does today.

**The pattern that makes it skippable.** A commit's diff is confined to the new node's directory plus one added, ticked line in the parent's order.md. That is all. Under that pattern the three things the toggle guards against cannot happen:

- **Code outside the node.** Impossible by construction, nothing outside changed.
- **An older file referencing the new node.** Same reason. A back-reference needs an edit outside the node.
- **The build breaking without the node.** The unticked build is the last release.

**When the pattern does not fit, the proof is mandatory.** A parent refactored to open an extension point, a refinement that also touched the parent, a regroup, a shared order.md reordered or a sibling unticked. Those are exactly the commits the toggle proof was written for, and they should keep it. The `--chains` diff stays for regroups.

**Where to enforce it.** Not in the worker's head. Two places:

- deploy.sh already lists the node directories each commit touched and the node specs it added. Extend that step to classify each commit as pattern-conforming or not, and fail the release when a non-conforming commit has no toggle proof recorded. The record can be one line in the commit message, or a proof marker the linker writes.
- A linker flag, say `fmlink.py miso --prove <node>`, that runs the same classification from the working tree before commit, so a worker learns in a second which kind of commit it is making.

**What it saves.** In machine time, two extra links and a rerun of the flows, cheap warm, around 17 seconds cold in each worktree. The real saving is a worker step and a hazard. The re-tick rule in CLAUDE.md exists because a transient untick once stayed in the shared file. The pattern check never touches order.md.

**Three cautions.**

- The argument rests on ship as built. If commits ever stack unreleased on main, the "previous commit was gated" premise fails. Then the check must find the last released commit, which the deploy stamp names, and use the range.
- A worktree on a stale base would pass the pattern and still be wrong. The worker preamble already demands a fast-forward first. The deploy check should verify the parent commit is main's tip.
- The unticked state is proven, but the ticked state is still only proven by the smoke gate and whatever flows the worker ran. This proposal removes nothing from that side.

I have written this into notes.md as a proposal, not a decision. If you say go, the work is one deploy.sh step and one linker flag, then agents.md step 4 gets rewritten to "fit the pattern, or prove the toggle".

The proposal is recorded in notes.md. To recap for you:

- **Skippable case.** A commit that touches only the new node's directory and adds one ticked line to the parent's order.md needs no toggle proof. The unticked build is identical to the last release, which was already gated.
- **Mandatory case.** Any commit that edits outside the node keeps the full proof. That is where the proof earns its keep.
- **Enforcement.** A classification step in deploy.sh, a `--prove` flag on the linker for the worker's own check, and a rewrite of agents.md step 4.
- **Premises.** Ship as built, a worker base that is main's tip, and the last commit having been released.

Say go and I'll build the two tool changes and rewrite step 4. Also still pending from before: the two uncommitted files, hybrid.md and the worker agent definition, and a session restart to make the new subagent settings live.
